title: CIPD Level 5
issuer: Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public CIPD Level 5 Associate Diploma syllabus (strategic people management, organisational performance, talent management, employment relations). Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: An organisation is developing a new five-year strategy that aims to expand into international markets. What should the HR function do FIRST to support this strategic direction?
options: Assess current workforce capabilities against the future skills needed for international expansion
Review and update all employee contracts to include international mobility clauses
Introduce a new performance management system across all departments
Conduct exit interviews to understand why employees are leaving the organisation
items.explanation: To support a new strategic direction, HR should first conduct a gap analysis between current capabilities and future skills needs to inform workforce planning and development priorities.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: A senior leadership team has asked HR to demonstrate how its initiatives contribute to the organisation's strategic objectives. Which approach would be MOST effective for measuring this?
options: Counting the total number of training days delivered each year
Linking HR key performance indicators directly to specific strategic objectives and outcomes
Tracking the percentage of job vacancies filled within 30 days
Monitoring the number of employees who attend HR information sessions
items.explanation: Aligning HR metrics to strategic objectives provides clear evidence of HR's contribution to business outcomes and helps to justify investment in people initiatives.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: When aligning HR strategy with business strategy in a rapidly changing environment, what is the key benefit of adopting a 'strategic partner' role for HR?
options: HR can focus solely on ensuring compliance with employment legislation
HR can reduce its workload by delegating tasks to line managers
HR can proactively shape people solutions that enable the organisation to respond to change
HR can standardise all policies regardless of business unit needs
items.explanation: As a strategic partner, HR works alongside leadership to anticipate challenges and develop proactive people solutions that support organisational agility and performance.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: An organisation is considering outsourcing some of its HR administration functions. What should be the PRIMARY consideration when evaluating this option?
options: Whether the outsourcing provider is the cheapest available option
How quickly the contract can be signed without negotiation
The geographical location of the outsourcing provider's offices
The impact on service quality, data security and the internal HR role
items.explanation: Outsourcing HR functions requires careful consideration of service standards, data protection compliance and how it will reshape the strategic role of internal HR.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: To effectively influence senior stakeholders on a proposed HR change initiative, what approach is MOST likely to gain their support?
options: Present a clear business case with data, risks and projected return on investment
Rely on highlighting the initiative's alignment with HR best practice
Emphasise that the change is required to meet HR policy requirements
Focus on how the initiative will improve HR's internal processes
items.explanation: Senior stakeholders are primarily focused on business outcomes, so presenting a robust business case with measurable benefits and risks is most persuasive.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: An organisation operating in a highly competitive market is facing skills shortages. What is the MOST sustainable long-term HR response?
options: Rely exclusively on temporary agency staff to fill all vacancies
Develop a comprehensive talent pipeline through apprenticeships and internal development
Freeze all hiring and redistribute work across existing staff indefinitely
Reduce entry requirements to fill positions as quickly as possible
items.explanation: Building a sustainable talent pipeline through development and early careers initiatives addresses skills shortages whilst supporting retention and organisational capability.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of vertical integration between HR and business strategy?
options: HR policies are applied consistently across all hierarchical levels
HR and finance functions share the same reporting structure
HR strategies directly support and drive the achievement of business strategic goals
All employees receive the same training regardless of their role
items.explanation: Vertical integration means HR strategy flows from and supports the overall business strategy, ensuring people initiatives enable strategic objectives.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: An organisation is implementing a major change programme. To manage the people implications effectively, what should HR prioritise FIRST?
options: Update the employee handbook with new policies
Organise a celebration event to mark the start of the change
Draft new job descriptions for all affected roles
Identify key stakeholders and assess their readiness for change
items.explanation: Conducting stakeholder analysis and readiness assessments at the outset allows HR to identify potential resistance and develop targeted change management interventions.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a HR business partner model within an organisation?
options: To provide strategic, tailored HR advice to business leaders whilst maintaining operational support
To centralise all HR decisions and remove line manager involvement
To focus exclusively on transactional HR processes
To ensure HR operates as an entirely independent function
items.explanation: The HRBP model balances strategic partnership with operational delivery, providing business-focused advice whilst supporting day-to-day people management.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: In the context of strategic workforce planning, what does the term 'demand forecasting' refer to?
options: Estimating the cost of employee benefits for the next financial year
Predicting the number and type of roles required to meet future business needs
Calculating annual leave entitlement across the workforce
Forecasting payroll expenditure based on current headcount
items.explanation: Demand forecasting involves projecting future workforce requirements based on business strategy, growth plans, and anticipated changes to work requirements.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: An organisation wants to develop a more inclusive workplace culture as part of its people strategy. What should be HR's MOST effective starting point?
options: Issue a statement from the CEO declaring the organisation is inclusive
Remove all references to diversity from internal communications
Conduct an equality impact assessment and gather workforce data to identify barriers
Only recruit from a single source to maintain consistency
items.explanation: Data-driven approaches, including equality impact assessments and workforce analysis, help identify actual barriers and inform targeted, measurable inclusion initiatives.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: When evaluating the effectiveness of an HR strategy, which of the following would provide the STRONGEST evidence of success?
options: A high number of likes on HR's internal social media posts
Increased attendance at HR-led wellbeing events
Positive feedback from HR staff about their workload
Demonstrable improvements in key business metrics linked to people initiatives
items.explanation: The strongest evidence of HR strategic effectiveness is measurable improvement in business outcomes, such as productivity, retention, or revenue growth linked to people initiatives.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: An organisation is considering a merger with another company. What is HR's PRIMARY responsibility during the due diligence phase?
options: Assessing people-related risks, including culture, contracts, and liabilities
Designing new corporate logos and branding materials
Selecting office furniture for the combined organisation
Negotiating supplier contracts for stationery and supplies
items.explanation: HR plays a critical role in due diligence by identifying workforce-related risks, including cultural fit, employment terms, pensions, and potential TUPE or redundancy implications.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: To build credibility as a strategic HR function, it is MOST important for HR professionals to develop which skill set?
options: Advanced knowledge of administrative procedures and filing systems
Commercial awareness combined with HR expertise and data analysis skills
Proficiency in formatting documents and managing calendars
Expertise in booking travel and processing expenses
items.explanation: Combining commercial awareness with HR knowledge and analytical capability enables HR to speak the language of the business and provide evidence-based strategic advice.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: Which approach BEST supports HR's role in promoting ethical practice within an organisation?
options: Keeping ethical concerns confidential and avoiding challenging senior leaders
Applying different ethical standards to different levels of the organisation
Embedding ethical principles into policies, decision-making frameworks and leadership behaviours
Prioritising commercial gain over employee wellbeing in all decisions
items.explanation: Embedding ethics into structures and behaviours helps ensure consistent, fair decision-making and reinforces an ethical organisational culture.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: An HR team wants to move from a reactive to a more proactive approach. What organisational enabler would MOST support this shift?
options: Restricting HR access to management information systems
Focusing exclusively on responding to employee queries
Recording data only at the end of each financial year
Access to timely workforce analytics and predictive data
items.explanation: Timely workforce data and analytics enable HR to identify trends, anticipate challenges, and take preventative action rather than simply reacting to issues.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: When managing multiple stakeholder interests during an HR strategy review, what is the MOST effective approach?
options: Identify shared priorities and find areas of mutual benefit before negotiating compromises
Prioritise the views of the most senior stakeholder above all others
Make a decision in isolation and communicate it after finalising details
Avoid consultation to prevent stakeholders from raising objections
items.explanation: Focusing on common goals and mutual benefit builds consensus and reduces conflict when balancing competing stakeholder interests.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: Which of the following BEST illustrates the concept of HR adding value to the business?
options: HR increasing the volume of paperwork processed each month
HR initiatives that directly improve organisational performance and employee outcomes
HR maintaining records for the sake of compliance alone
HR enforcing rules without considering business context
items.explanation: HR adds value when its work leads to measurable improvements in both business performance and positive employee experiences.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Strategic People Management

items.stem: An organisation has noticed declining employee engagement scores over the past two years. What should be the FIRST step to address this issue?
options: Implement a company-wide pay increase immediately
Introduce a new dress code policy
Conduct a thorough analysis of survey results to identify underlying causes
Reduce annual leave entitlement to improve productivity
items.explanation: Analysing survey data helps identify specific drivers of disengagement, allowing targeted interventions rather than generic solutions.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of organisational culture?
options: The formal structure outlined in the organisational chart
The physical layout of office premises
The IT systems used across the organisation
The shared values, beliefs and behaviours that shape how work is done
items.explanation: Organisational culture reflects unwritten norms and shared assumptions that influence employee attitudes and behaviours.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: To improve organisational performance, a line manager wants to create a high-trust team environment. What is the MOST effective approach?
options: Demonstrate consistency, transparency and follow through on commitments
Share confidential information about colleagues
Favour certain team members when allocating opportunities
Avoid giving constructive feedback to prevent conflict
items.explanation: Building trust requires leaders to act with integrity, be transparent and consistently deliver on their promises.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: An organisation is experiencing high levels of workplace stress. Which HR intervention would be MOST effective in addressing the root cause?
options: Offer free gym membership to all employees
Conduct a stress risk assessment to identify and mitigate workplace stressors
Provide relaxation music in communal areas
Distribute stress balls to staff
items.explanation: A stress risk assessment, following HSE management standards principles, identifies organisational stressors and enables preventative action.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: What is the PRIMARY benefit of effective performance management?
options: It allows managers to rank employees for redundancy purposes
It ensures all employees receive identical ratings
It aligns individual performance with organisational goals and supports development
It removes the need for regular feedback conversations
items.explanation: Effective performance management focuses on goal alignment, ongoing feedback and development to drive organisational performance.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: An organisation wants to embed its values into day-to-day behaviour. What is the MOST impactful approach?
options: Include values only in the employee induction handbook
Display values posters in reception with no further action
Discuss values once a year at the annual conference
Recognise and reward behaviours that demonstrate the stated values
items.explanation: Reinforcing values through recognition and reward ensures they are lived rather than simply stated.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: Which of the following would BEST indicate a healthy psychological safety climate?
options: Team members feel safe to raise concerns and admit mistakes without fear of blame
Employees avoid challenging ideas to maintain harmony
Mistakes are punished harshly to prevent recurrence
Only senior staff are allowed to voice opinions in meetings
items.explanation: Psychological safety enables open dialogue, learning from mistakes and innovation, all of which support performance.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: A department consistently meets its targets but has very low morale. What should the manager focus on to achieve sustainable performance?
options: Increasing targets further to maintain momentum
Balancing results with employee wellbeing and development
Ignoring morale as long as targets are met
Pressuring staff to work longer hours
items.explanation: Sustainable performance requires attending to both productivity and wellbeing to avoid burnout and turnover.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: What is the key purpose of organisational change management?
options: To minimise communication about the change
To implement change as quickly as possible regardless of impact
To help people transition successfully through change to achieve desired outcomes
To avoid involving employees in the change process
items.explanation: Change management focuses on the human side of change, supporting adoption and minimising resistance.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: To measure the impact of a wellbeing initiative, which metric would be MOST meaningful?
options: Total number of wellbeing flyers distributed
Number of employees who liked a wellbeing post online
Cost of printing wellbeing materials
Reduction in sickness absence rates linked to stress-related reasons
items.explanation: Measurable outcomes such as stress-related absence provide evidence of an initiative's effectiveness.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: An organisation is seeking to become more agile. What cultural shift would BEST support this?
options: Encouraging experimentation, learning and empowered decision-making
Requiring multiple layers of approval for all decisions
Punishing failed attempts to discourage risk-taking
Maintaining rigid hierarchies and fixed processes
items.explanation: Agility requires a culture that empowers employees, tolerates intelligent failure and supports continuous learning.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: Which of the following BEST describes employee voice?
options: A system for recording attendance only
Mechanisms that enable employees to express views and influence decisions
A process for issuing formal warnings
An annual pay review procedure
items.explanation: Employee voice gives employees meaningful opportunities to contribute ideas and shape decisions affecting their work.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: A merger has created two distinct subcultures with conflicting norms. What should HR do FIRST to address this?
options: Enforce one culture by dismissing opposing views
Let the cultures evolve naturally with no intervention
Facilitate dialogue to identify shared values and common ground
Separate the teams permanently
items.explanation: Creating a shared sense of purpose through dialogue helps integrate cultures constructively and reduce conflict.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: What is the MOST effective way to reinforce desired behaviours across an organisation?
options: Rely solely on line manager discretion
Include desired behaviours in a policy document only
Communicate them once via email
Align recruitment, induction, performance and reward practices with desired behaviours
items.explanation: Consistency across people processes ensures behaviours are embedded systematically, not ad hoc.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: An organisation wants to improve its diversity and inclusion outcomes. Which approach would have the GREATEST long-term impact?
options: Addressing systemic barriers through policy, process and cultural change
Setting quotas without changing underlying processes
Running a one-off unconscious bias training session
Highlighting diversity only during annual celebrations
items.explanation: Sustainable change requires tackling structural and cultural barriers, not just awareness-raising alone.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Organisational Performance and Culture

items.stem: In workforce planning, 'supply analysis' refers to which of the following?
options: Calculating projected sales revenue
Assessing the skills and availability of the current and future workforce
Estimating competitor market share
Forecasting raw material costs
items.explanation: Supply analysis examines internal and external talent availability to identify gaps against future requirements.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: What is the PRIMARY objective of a talent management strategy?
options: To reduce headcount across all departments
To standardise job titles throughout the organisation
To attract, develop and retain the talent needed to deliver business strategy
To eliminate all external recruitment
items.explanation: Talent management ensures the organisation has the right people with the right skills to achieve strategic goals.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: An organisation identifies high-potential employees as part of its succession planning. What should be the NEXT step?
options: Automatically promote them to senior positions
Exclude them from their current responsibilities
Reduce their performance targets
Create individual development plans tailored to future roles
items.explanation: Targeted development plans prepare high-potentials for future roles whilst building their capabilities.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a skills gap analysis?
options: Comparing required skills for a role against current employee capabilities
Comparing salaries across similar roles
Reviewing employee attendance records
Analysing office space utilisation
items.explanation: A skills gap analysis identifies specific capability shortfalls to inform learning and recruitment priorities.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: To attract diverse talent, what is the MOST effective recruitment approach?
options: Advertise roles only through personal networks
Use inclusive job adverts, diverse sourcing channels and structured interviews
Use informal, unstructured interviews for all candidates
Rely solely on word-of-mouth referrals
items.explanation: Inclusive practices reduce bias and widen the talent pool to attract more diverse candidates.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: What is the key benefit of internal talent mobility?
options: It increases recruitment agency fees
It creates unnecessary competition between colleagues
It supports retention, development and faster filling of critical roles
It prevents employees from gaining new experiences
items.explanation: Internal mobility builds loyalty, develops skills and reduces time-to-fill for key positions.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: An ageing workforce is presenting retention challenges. What would be a pragmatic HR response?
options: Enforce mandatory retirement at a fixed age
Exclude older workers from training opportunities
Reduce benefits for long-serving employees
Offer flexible working, career development and phased retirement options
items.explanation: Flexible approaches support retention, knowledge transfer and workforce planning for demographic change.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: Which of the following is the MOST reliable predictor of future performance in selection?
options: A structured interview based on job-related competencies
The candidate's appearance and demeanour
Personal connections with the hiring manager
Preference based on shared interests
items.explanation: Structured, competency-based interviews have higher validity and reliability than unstructured approaches.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of onboarding beyond induction?
options: To collect emergency contact details only
To help new starters integrate culturally and become productive quickly
To issue a building access pass
To complete paperwork before day one
items.explanation: Effective onboarding supports social integration, role clarity and accelerates productivity.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: An organisation wants to reduce early leaver rates for graduates. What initiative would be MOST effective?
options: Give graduates minimal support and high workloads
Rotate them between roles with no guidance
Provide a structured buddy, mentoring and development programme
Leave them to learn entirely through observation
items.explanation: Structured support improves engagement and increases retention of early careers hires.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: In workforce planning, what does 'scenario planning' help to address?
options: Predicting a single exact outcome with certainty
Avoiding contingency planning altogether
Focusing only on best-case projections
Preparing for multiple possible futures under different conditions
items.explanation: Scenario planning enables flexible responses by considering alternative future workforce scenarios.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: Which of the following BEST supports knowledge transfer when experienced employees retire?
options: Establish mentoring, job shadowing and documented processes
Remove all access to their files on departure
Rely on verbal handovers with no records
Ask them to leave without knowledge sharing
items.explanation: Systematic knowledge transfer preserves critical expertise and reduces organisational risk.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: What is the MOST important consideration when designing a learning and development strategy?
options: Selecting the most expensive training provider
Aligning learning with business priorities and identified skills gaps
Offering the same course to every employee
Delivering training regardless of relevance
items.explanation: Learning and development must address capability gaps that directly support strategic and operational goals.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: To measure the return on investment of a leadership development programme, what would be the BEST approach?
options: Count total attendance on the day
Ask participants if they enjoyed the food
Track behavioural change, promotion rates and business impact over time
Measure how many handouts were printed
items.explanation: Meaningful ROI assessment looks at sustained behaviour change and tangible business outcomes.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: An organisation faces critical skills shortages in a niche area. What is the MOST sustainable response?
options: Depend entirely on premium agency rates long-term
Delay projects indefinitely
Ignore the shortage and hope it resolves
Build internal capability through targeted development and knowledge sharing
items.explanation: Developing internal talent is more sustainable and cost-effective than perpetual external hiring.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Talent Management and Workforce Planning

items.stem: Under UK employment law, what is the key difference between an employee and a worker?
options: Employees have greater statutory rights, including unfair dismissal protection in most cases
Workers are entitled to the same pension as employees in all cases
There is no legal distinction between them
Employees have no right to holiday pay
items.explanation: The distinction affects entitlement to key rights; employees generally have stronger protections than workers.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of an employment contract?
options: To replace all company policies
To set out the terms and conditions of employment between parties
To guarantee a pay rise every year
To prevent employees from leaving the organisation
items.explanation: A contract defines rights, obligations and key terms, providing clarity and legal protection for both parties.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: An employee raises a grievance. What should the employer do FIRST?
options: Dismiss the employee immediately
Ignore the complaint until it escalates
Acknowledge the grievance and follow the formal grievance procedure
Discuss it publicly in a team meeting
items.explanation: Prompt acknowledgement and following a fair procedure is essential to resolve grievances lawfully and fairly.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: Which of the following BEST describes indirect discrimination under equality legislation?
options: Someone is overtly called names at work
An individual is refused a job because of their race
An employee is assaulted due to their religion
A provision, criterion or practice disadvantages a protected group disproportionately
items.explanation: Indirect discrimination is often unintentional but still unlawful if it cannot be objectively justified.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: What is the MINIMUM statutory notice period for an employee with two years' continuous service?
options: One week
One day
No notice required
Two months
items.explanation: Under UK law, statutory minimum notice increases with service length, starting at one week after one month of continuous service.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: Which of the following is a key principle of fair disciplinary action?
options: Decisions are made based on hearsay alone
The employee has the right to know the case against them and respond
No investigation is needed for serious allegations
The employee is not allowed representation
items.explanation: Natural justice requires a fair investigation, clear allegations, opportunity to respond and consideration of representation.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: Under the Working Time Regulations, what is the maximum average working week (excluding opt-outs)?
options: 40 hours
35 hours
48 hours
37.5 hours
items.explanation: The Working Time Regulations generally limit average weekly working time to 48 hours unless the worker has opted out.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: What is the significance of 'continuity of employment'?
options: It only affects pension scheme membership fees
It determines the office car parking allocation
It has no legal relevance
It determines eligibility for many statutory rights
items.explanation: Continuity affects rights such as unfair dismissal, redundancy pay and statutory notice periods.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: When managing a redundancy situation, what is the MOST important legal requirement?
options: Following a fair and objective selection process with consultation
Selecting employees based on personal preference
Making decisions without consulting affected staff
Telling employees on the same day as the decision
items.explanation: Fair selection, genuine redundancy and meaningful consultation are key to avoiding unfair dismissal claims.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: What does 'TUPE' primarily protect?
options: Share options only
Employees' terms and conditions when a business transfers to a new employer
Company car allowances in all circumstances
Personal email addresses
items.explanation: The Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations protect employment rights on relevant transfers.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: An employer receives a flexible working request. What is the correct response timeframe?
options: 24 hours
One week
Three months to respond (in most cases under current legislation)
No specific timeframe
items.explanation: Employers must consider requests reasonably and respond within three months, including any appeal process.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law

items.stem: Which of the following BEST demonstrates reasonable adjustments under the Equality Act 2010?
options: Refusing all changes to standard procedures
Treating disabled employees exactly the same in all cases
Expecting disabled employees to work without support
Modifying working arrangements or equipment to remove substantial disadvantage
items.explanation: Reasonable adjustments remove barriers to enable disabled employees to work on an equal basis.
items.reference: CIPD Level 5 Syllabus - Employment Relationship and Law
